title: chart-doors-refuse-in-one-pass
intention: The seven chart validate_* gates refuse complete in one pass — every lack accumulated and raised once, every floor refusal naming the command that produces the missing artifact, and DoorRefused rendering field: why — so a refusal costs one fix-and-refire, not three to five round trips per stage.
why: Rank 2 (+7 folded in) of notes/2026-08-02-opus-compatibility-pass.json, ruled spec by 2026-08-03-projections-stand: a weaker model fires write_survey, fixes the one lack the refusal named, fires again, and meets a NEW refusal — three to five round trips per stage, seven stages deep, every extra trip a turn to wander in. orient.py even raises INSIDE a field loop. Meanwhile all six copied docstrings claim 'Refusals are loud and complete on first pass' — a false claim standing in code. The fix pattern is proven in-house twice (learning_block.check_input walks the whole contract; verdict.unanswered accumulates everything): seven doors close on one shape.
traces_to: Law 7 — errors are loud AND complete at diagnostic surfaces (the complete-diagnostic-on-first-pass method)

proves_green.proof_gate: proof teeth beside the code (cairn/machines/chart/proofs/), run bare twice, sealed under the tester (netns), validation persisted beside the code
proves_green.entry_gate: BUILDME rides the chart chain + intent berth + sorted berth
proves_green.durability_gate: not done until proven AND committed (git)

falsifier.proves_red: RED if: firing the same multi-defective packet at any of the seven gates twice learns a lack on the second pass the first did not name; or any docstring claims one-pass completeness while its code cascades; or str(DoorRefused) drops the whys; or the composed-judge layer's behavior changes (the judges were already one-pass — only the shape tiers convert).
falsifier.horizon: the next /chart voyage runs under the converted gates — its refusal round-trips are the lived measure
